posts.cooked: Command substituition is used. Example has been given for output of ps aux and sort -k10,10 -rn.

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
Correct option is c

We use the kill command which requires PID to kill the process which is taking the max CPU time and the user is not root. So, we use $( ... ) which is command substitution which will output the PID.

Now to get the PID we run ps -aux that gives the pid, user, etc for the running commands. We need to sort the output and remove root user from the list. After that we find the topmost command and return its PID.

Here is the detailed solution -

  • (a) - head -1 takes only the header line, so the actual process list is lost
  • (b) - Same as option (c) but uses -n option. With -n, sort treats TIME as numeric but TIME contains : so using numeric sort will fail and processes will not be sorted correctly by TIME
  • (c) - This option is correct because -
    • sed 1d deletes the header
    • sorted by TIME (-k10,10 -r, reverse) k10,10 means sort by 10th field only
    • grep -v '^root\b’ removes root-owned processes
    • head -1 picks the top one
    • awk '{print $2}' extracts PID
  • (d) - Header line is not removed before sorting, so header also gets sorted into the list. Then sed 1d deletes the first row after sorting, which may accidentally delete a valid process instead of the header

Check this session - @30:00 (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1lQezZlPuhXwF9HwIGeOxZoYABTKiKtEO/view)
